subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Much ado about nothing

options.text: Doing a lot and getting nothing in return
Making a big fuss over a small thing

solution:
The correct answer is **'Making a big fuss over a small thing '.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• ** **Given Idiom: ***Much ado about nothing*** refers to **excessive excitement or fuss about something that is of little importance.**

 
 
• **Example: ***This really isn't a big deal, it's all ****much ado about nothing.***
 
 
 
• ***​***From the given options, the **second option** is** **the** most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.**
 
• **Hence,** the correct answer is **option 2.**

**​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• ***The idiom/phrase originates from***: Much ado has been used to refer to a large commotion or excitement since the early part of the 1500s. However, Shakespeare popularized the current idiom by using it as the title of a comedy first performed in 1612
